# Badge

A short label for a status, category or count, next to what it describes.

<p class="odv-compstatus"><span class="odv-pill">In Multi-brand</span></p>

## See it live

<div class="odv-live"><span class="odv-wait">Start Storybook to see it live: <code>npm run storybook</code></span><iframe src="http://localhost:6006/iframe.html?id=components-badge--examples&viewMode=story&globals=scheme:multi-brand--aster;mode:light" title="Badge examples in Storybook" loading="lazy"></iframe><div class="bar"><span>Live from Storybook</span><a href="http://localhost:6006/?path=/docs/components-badge--docs">Open Badge in Storybook</a><a href="http://localhost:6006/iframe.html?id=components-badge--examples&viewMode=story&globals=scheme:multi-brand--aster;mode:dark">See it in dark</a></div></div>

## When to use it

**In Multi-brand:** Plan and status labels.

- **Use it when:** A state people scan for in a list or table, or a small category label.
- **Not when:** A message people must read (alert or toast), or an action (a button).

Instead:

- [Alert](./alert.md): A message, not a label.
- [Button](./button.md): Something to press.

## How Multi-brand uses it

<div class="odv-grid two"><div class="odv-dd"><div class="stage"><div class="odv-eyebrow">A status</div><div style="margin-top:6px"><b style="color:var(--color-status-success)">Use</b> Badge with a word</div><div><b style="color:var(--color-status-danger)">Not</b> A brand color as status</div></div><div class="cap">Brand hues vary, so meaning needs a word.</div></div><div class="odv-dd"><div class="stage"><div class="odv-eyebrow">Shape of a status badge</div><div style="margin-top:6px"><b style="color:var(--color-status-success)">Use</b> radius.badge (set by the brand)</div><div><b style="color:var(--color-status-danger)">Not</b> A hard-coded shape</div></div><div class="cap">The brand sets the badge shape.</div></div></div>

## Why it works this way

Badge looks the way it does because of 3 answers about this product. Each card is one answer, in three steps: the answer, what it decided for Badge, and what would move if it changed.

<section class="odv-trail" id="why-accessibility-count"><div class="odv-trail-head"><b>How many signals carry each meaning?</b><code>accessibility.count</code></div><div class="odv-steps"><div class="odv-step-col"><h5><i>1</i>The answer</h5><div class="odv-answer">Two: color and word</div><p>Brand colors vary, so meaning needs a word.</p></div><div class="odv-step-col"><h5><i>2</i>So Badge</h5><ul><li><span class="y">✓</span><span>uses <b>neutral</b>: Trial: the plan works and billing has not started.</span></li><li><span class="y">✓</span><span>uses <b>info</b>: Renews in 3 days: a payment is coming; nothing has gone wrong.</span></li><li><span class="y">✓</span><span>uses <b>success</b>: Active: the plan is paid and running.</span></li><li><span class="n">–</span><span>does not use <b>warning</b>: No plan or order state sits between running and failed; a coming renewal is news, not a warning.</span></li><li><span class="y">✓</span><span>uses <b>danger</b>: Card declined: the payment failed, so the plan will stop.</span></li></ul><div class="odv-also"><small>It also shapes</small> <code>Alert: destructive</code></div></div><div class="odv-step-col change"><h5><i>3</i>If it changed</h5><div class="odv-big">5</div><small>Badge decisions would reopen</small><p>No other answer follows from it.</p></div></div></section>

<section class="odv-trail" id="why-content-q1"><div class="odv-trail-head"><b>What is the main content?</b><code>content.q1</code></div><div class="odv-steps"><div class="odv-step-col"><h5><i>1</i>The answer</h5><div class="odv-answer">Forms and tasks</div><p>Product pages, sign-up and account forms.</p></div><div class="odv-step-col"><h5><i>2</i>So Badge</h5><ul><li><span class="n">–</span><span>does not use <b>warning</b>: No plan or order state sits between running and failed; a coming renewal is news, not a warning.</span></li></ul><div class="odv-also"><small>It also shapes</small> <code>Alert: default</code> <code>Input group: inline-start</code> <code>Input group: inline-end</code> <code>Input group: block-start</code> <code>Input group: block-end</code> <code>Item: outline</code></div></div><div class="odv-step-col change"><h5><i>3</i>If it changed</h5><div class="odv-big">1</div><small>Badge decision would reopen</small><p>and 9 answers that follow from it: <b>A moderate amount</b>, <b>Gaps, insets and row heights</b>, <b>Comfortable</b>, and 6 more.</p></div></div></section>

<section class="odv-trail" id="why-outcomes-q2"><div class="odv-trail-head"><b>What is a costly mistake?</b><code>outcomes.q2</code></div><div class="odv-steps"><div class="odv-step-col"><h5><i>1</i>The answer</h5><div class="odv-answer">Looking off-brand</div><p>A page that looks like the wrong brand loses trust.</p></div><div class="odv-step-col"><h5><i>2</i>So Badge</h5><ul><li><span class="y">✓</span><span>uses <b>danger</b>: Card declined: the payment failed, so the plan will stop.</span></li></ul><div class="odv-also"><small>It also shapes</small> <code>Button: secondary</code> <code>Button: danger</code> <code>Alert: destructive</code></div></div><div class="odv-step-col change"><h5><i>3</i>If it changed</h5><div class="odv-big">1</div><small>Badge decision would reopen</small><p>and 1 answer that follow from it: <b>Also for emphasis and size</b>.</p></div></div></section>

## Words

- Shared structure: object, state, next step.
- Brand tone lives in headlines and marketing copy, not in errors.
- Errors and confirmations read the same in every brand.
- Use: Get started, Plan, Order. Avoid: Brand-specific words in errors, Jargon.

The labels components use, from the voice tokens:

- `content.action.commit`: Save
- `content.action.cancel`: Cancel
- `content.action.destroy`: Remove
- `content.action.retry`: Try again
- `content.action.empty-action`: Get started

See [Voice and tone](../voice.md) for the whole voice.

## Accessibility and keyboard

Test before you ship:

- [ ] The status is a word; color and icon add to it, never replace it. undefined

## Use it in code

```bash
npx open-ds add badge
```

The component reads only component keys and semantic tokens, so it follows the brand and mode on `<html>`.

## Tokens it reads

Badge reads 13 tokens of its own, each an alias of a semantic token. Each row is one part: its own token, the semantic it aliases, and the value it ends at. A row marked Themeable changes between light and dark. Change a semantic and every component that reads it follows; override one of Badge's tokens to change Badge alone.
